---
title: "Glossary"
aliases:
  - /background.html
---

| Term | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| loading ($\phi$) | The loading measures how strongly a claim's dividend growth moves with the persistent component of consumption. The loading is the model's characteristic, and it is measured from cash flows. |
| persistent component ($x_t$) | The persistent component is the deviation of expected consumption growth from its mean, and the deviation decays slowly. |
| half-life | The half-life is the time for a shock to $x_t$ to decay by half. It equals $\log(0.5)/\log(\rho)$, and it is about 34 months at $\rho = 0.98$. |
| P/D ratio | The P/D ratio is the price per unit of annual dividend, and the log of the P/D ratio is the valuation measure. |
| beta | Beta is the slope of a claim's return on the market's return in the CAPM. |
| EIS ($\psi$) | The EIS is the elasticity of intertemporal substitution, and it is the response of consumption plans to interest rates. |
| risk aversion ($\gamma$) | Risk aversion is the willingness to pay to avoid consumption risk. |
| $\theta$ | $\theta$ is the Epstein-Zin composite $(1-\gamma)/(1-1/\psi)$, and the distance of $\theta$ from 1 measures how far the preferences are from power utility. |
| pricing kernel / stochastic discount factor ($M$) | The pricing kernel is the household's intertemporal marginal rate of substitution, and every claim is priced through $E_t[M_{t+1} R_{i,t+1}] = 1$. |
| Euler equation | The Euler equation is $E_t[M_{t+1}R_{i,t+1}]=1$, so every asset's return, weighted by the household's marginal utility, has expected value one. |
| cash-flow news | Cash-flow news is a revision in expected dividends. |
| discount-rate news | Discount-rate news is a revision in expected returns. |
| log-linearization | Log-linearization is the approximation $r_{t+1} \approx \text{const} + \Delta d_{t+1} + \kappa_1 z_{t+1} - z_t$, and the approximation makes the valuation ratio linear in the state. |
| $\kappa_1$ | $\kappa_1$ is the log-linearization constant $e^{\bar z}/(1+e^{\bar z})$, near 0.997, and it discounts next period's valuation ratio. |

The formulas are in [Mathematical detail](../lrr/math.qmd).
A reference list is in [References](references.qmd).
